The defendant, Ng Sui-ting, appeared in court this morning wearing a green polo shirt, beige shorts, and a black mask. The charges allege that on July 10 and August 17 respectively, the defendant allowed a male yellow mixed-breed dog, without being restrained by a leash not exceeding two metres in length, to enter the vicinity of YOHO Mall in Yuen Long, and is charged with two counts of "permitting a large dog to enter or remain in a public place."

The prosecution applied for the case to be adjourned for ten weeks before the next mention, and did not oppose bail. Acting Principal Magistrate Shao Siu-hung agreed to adjourn the case to October 29 for mention, and the defendant was granted bail.

According to the Dangerous Dogs Regulation, "permitting a large dog to enter or remain in a public place," upon conviction, carries a fine of HK$25,000 and imprisonment for three months.

Assistant Director of the Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department (AFCD) Yip Yin said yesterday that if the dog owner decides to surrender the large dog to the government, the department would consider methods including humane euthanasia; if the owner intends to take the dog back, the dog may be classified as a "known dangerous dog," and the court may order that the dog must wear a muzzle whenever going out in the future.

Kent, founder of the animal protection organisation Mow Mow Rescue, told The Collective that the dog owner regrets signing the surrender form; he also said Mow Mow is willing to take in the dog and provide a dog trainer for behavioural rehabilitation.
